cards.title: CLI login fails with project API key
cards.summary: When `composio link`, CLI login, or MCP setup fails with 401 Invalid API key and the visible key prefix is `ak_...`, the likely issue is that the user supplied a project API key where the CLI/user-auth flow expects a User API Key.
symptoms: `composio link` fails with 401 Invalid API key
Error mentions CLI, MCP login, or local auth setup
The redacted key preview starts with `ak_...`
The user says they copied an API key from project settings
likelyCauses: A project API key is being used for a user-level CLI or MCP login flow
The current key was rotated, revoked, truncated, or copied with extra whitespace
`AUTH_CONFIG_ID` may be an integration ID instead of the `ac_...` auth config ID
fixes: Use the User API Key for CLI and MCP login flows; it should use the user-key surface rather than the project-key surface
Use project API keys for project REST API calls that expect project authentication
Keep `AUTH_CONFIG_ID` as the `ac_...` auth config ID, not the integration ID
If the retry still fails, ask for the new request ID from the CLI error
whenToUse: Use when the support request mentions CLI login, `composio link`, MCP auth, or local setup with a 401 Invalid API key
Use when the supplied redacted key prefix is `ak_...` and the requested operation is user-level auth
requiredEvidence: Command or surface being used, such as CLI, MCP, REST API, or dashboard
Redacted key prefix only, never the full key
Request ID if the suggested key-type fix does not work
avoidMentioning: Do not ask for the full API key
Do not ask for unrelated provider headers before addressing key type
Do not mention unrelated toolkits or prior cases

cards.title: Pipedrive connection fails when company domain is a full URL
cards.summary: For Pipedrive auth/configuration, the company domain field should be the company slug only, not a full URL and not a hostname with `.pipedrive.com`.
symptoms: Pipedrive connection or remote tool execution fails with SSRF or DNS resolution errors
Error says DNS resolution failed for `https` or hostname verification failed
The dashboard may show the connected account as active while remote execution fails
likelyCauses: The company domain field contains a full URL or full hostname instead of the Pipedrive company slug
The URL parser treats part of the scheme or malformed host as the hostname, triggering SSRF protection
fixes: Set the Pipedrive company domain field to the slug only, for example `acme`
Do not include `https://`, `http://`, or `.pipedrive.com` in the company domain field
Retry the connection or tool execution after updating the domain format
whenToUse: Use when Pipedrive errors mention SSRF, DNS resolution, hostname verification, or `ExternalProxy_SSRFBlocked`
Use when a customer says Pipedrive is active in the dashboard but remote execution fails
requiredEvidence: Request ID only if the format fix does not resolve the issue
avoidMentioning: Do not ask for tokens or credentials
Do not imply the exact request ID was found unless diagnostics confirm it
Do not claim a spike or platform issue from broad logs alone

cards.title: Gmail managed OAuth app blocks gmail.modify scope
cards.summary: If Google blocks a Gmail connection after adding `gmail.modify`, the issue may be scope approval on the managed app. A broader approved mail scope can be used where appropriate, or the customer can use custom Google credentials and complete Google's review.
symptoms: Gmail OAuth shows an app blocked message
The customer wants to avoid custom Google credential review
likelyCauses: The managed Gmail OAuth app does not have approval for the requested restricted scope
Google is enforcing verification requirements for the configured scope set
fixes: Use an approved managed Gmail scope if it satisfies the product need
Use custom Google OAuth credentials when the app needs scopes that require the customer's own Google review
Keep the response clear that this is a Google scope approval constraint, not a connected-account runtime failure
whenToUse: Use when Gmail OAuth is blocked after adding Gmail write or modify scopes
Use when the customer asks whether something changed on Composio's side for Google verification
requiredEvidence: Whether the customer is using Composio-managed or custom OAuth credentials
avoidMentioning: Do not promise managed-app approval for a scope unless confirmed
Do not ask for logs before checking the configured scope and auth mode

cards.title: Monday OAuth requires workspace app installation
cards.summary: Monday may show an app-not-installed error until a Monday workspace admin installs the Composio app for the workspace. After installation, users can retry the connection.
symptoms: Monday connection shows `App is not installed`
The error appears during integration or OAuth setup
A non-admin user is trying to authorize before workspace installation
likelyCauses: Monday requires the app to be installed by a workspace admin before users can authorize it
The workspace has not approved or installed the app yet
fixes: Ask a Monday workspace admin to install and approve the app for the workspace
Retry the Monday connection in Composio after the app is installed
If it still fails, ask for the workspace name and a fresh screenshot after the install attempt
whenToUse: Use when monday.com OAuth or integration setup reports that the app is not installed
requiredEvidence: Whether a Monday workspace admin has installed the app
Workspace name if the error persists after admin install
avoidMentioning: Do not ask for Monday credentials
Do not treat this as a Composio outage before checking the Monday workspace prerequisite
